# What the data-dict export loses: Current Population Survey, Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2019` | `2020` | `2021` | `2022` | `2023` | `2024` | `2025` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 |
| table references whose `when` condition is only in a description, and whose columns aren't marked foreign_key | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| links between releases, not exported | 246 | 246 | 246 | 246 | 246 | 246 | 246 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
